definition: Antiquated means old and out of date.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word antiquated. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know antiquated should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The hotel's antiquated switchboard still routes calls through brass plugs, and only one retired operator understands its wiring.
Dated is the milder judgment — a dated kitchen shows its age but cooks dinner fine; antiquated says the age has started costing you.
Extinct goes further than antiquated: antiquated equipment still runs, badly out of step with the present, while an extinct technology has disappeared from use altogether.

Outmoded means pushed aside by newer ways of doing the job, and it points at the method or the fashion — an outmoded technique, an outmoded cut of suit. Antiquated aims at the whole thing — machine, system, law — and adds that its age has begun costing you.

Old-school describes older ways kept on with a wink of respect — an old-school barber, an old-school defense. The age is a feature, savored on purpose. Antiquated turns the same age into a complaint: the thing has fallen behind, and keeping it going has started to cost.

Antiquated is the right word because it means old and out of date — old in a way that no longer serves.
Age alone does not qualify: a cast-iron pan from the same era still works beautifully and is merely old.
